text: Distributed training moves tensors between workers while a controller coordinates communication stages. This synthetic artifact sample is repeated by the infinite training data loader and is intended only for a short systems smoke test.

Pipeline parallel workers exchange activations and gradients between neighboring stages. The emulation run checks that communication requests reach the Opus controller and receive configuration acknowledgements.

Tensor parallel workers cooperate on matrix operations within each model layer. Network collectives remain on the native cluster fabric while the control plane injects a configurable logical reconfiguration delay.
Data parallel workers synchronize model gradients after local computation. The artifact uses a deterministic local text dataset so evaluators do not need to download the complete C4 training corpus.

A successful evaluation initializes all ranks, creates process groups, loads batches, executes forward and backward passes, and reports training metrics. Controller logs independently record topology requests and acknowledgements.
Perlmutter GPU nodes expose the Slingshot network to NCCL through the site container runtime. The launcher starts one torchrun agent per node and four Python ranks per agent for this experiment.

Optical rail emulation models control-plane timing without changing the physical cluster network. This distinction lets the software path be reproduced even when the original optical circuit switch is unavailable.

Artifact evaluation favors small deterministic inputs and explicit logs. These sentences provide enough tokenizable input for repeated batches while keeping the repository lightweight and the run independent of external datasets.
